subject: maths
title: Year 4 Rounding and Estimation
seo_title: Year 4 Rounding and Estimation Worksheets: Free Maths with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Choose and use estimation and rounding to check and explain the reasonableness of calculations including the results of financial transactions
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on rounding and estimation, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4N07): round to the nearest 10, 100 and 1000 on number lines, estimate sums, differences and products, check if answers are reasonable, round prices to the nearest dollar and round cash to the nearest 5c. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: To round, look at the digit to the right: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down. 450 rounds to 500.
key_sub: Estimate before you calculate: 38 × 4 is about 40 × 4 = 160. If your answer is far from the estimate, check it. When you pay cash, round the total to the nearest 5c.
body_html:
Rounding: find the closer friendly number

To round, find the two friendly numbers on each side. Then look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to. 5 or more rounds up. 4 or less rounds down.

Round to the nearestLook at theExample
10ones digit365 → 370
100tens digit1749 → 1700
1000hundreds digit4682 → 5000
Exactly halfway

Round 450 to the nearest 100.

450 is exactly halfway between 400 and 500. A number exactly halfway rounds up.

Answer: 500

A 9 that rounds up

Round 3962 to the nearest 100.

Look at the tens digit: 6, so round up. 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds = 1 thousand.

Answer: 4000

Estimate, then check

An estimate is a quick answer that is close to the exact answer. Round the numbers, then work it out in your head. If your exact answer is far from the estimate, check your working.

Estimate a sum

Estimate 347 + 486.

Round to the nearest 100: 300 + 500 = 800. The exact answer is 833, which is close.

Answer: about 800

Estimate a product

Estimate 38 × 4.

38 rounds to 40. 40 × 4 = 160. The exact answer is 152. 38 was rounded up, so the estimate is a bit too big.

Answer: about 160

Is the answer reasonable?

Jack says 4 × 76 = 2824.

Estimate: 4 × 80 = 320. 2824 is far too big, so it is not reasonable. The exact answer is 304.

Answer: not reasonable

Estimating with money

Round each price to the nearest dollar. 50c or more rounds up; less than 50c rounds down.

Paying cash: round to the nearest 5c

Australia has no 1c or 2c coins. When you pay with cash, the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. If you pay by card, you pay the exact amount.

Cash change

The bill is $8.62. You pay cash with a $10 note.

Round the total first: $8.62 → $8.60. Then $10 − $8.60 = $1.40.

Answer: $1.40

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Looking at the wrong digit: 1749 to the nearest 100 → 1750For the nearest 100, look at the tens digit: 4, so 1700
Rounding 450 down to 400Exactly halfway rounds up: 500
Always rounding down: 682 → 600The tens digit is 8 (5 or more), so round up: 700
Rounding in steps: 6499 → 6500 → 7000Look only at the hundreds digit: 4, so 6000
Not checking: 3 × 214 = 6312Estimate 3 × 200 = 600; 6312 is far too big. The answer is 642

faq.q: What does Year 4 learn about rounding and estimation in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 4 students choose and use estimation and rounding to check whether answers are reasonable, including money amounts (AC9M4N07). They round to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000 and estimate sums, differences and products.
To the nearest 100, 450 rounds to 500. A number exactly halfway between two hundreds is rounded up.

faq.q: How does rounding to the nearest 5 cents work in Australia?
faq.a: Cash totals are rounded because there are no 1c or 2c coins. Totals ending in 1 or 2 round down to 0, 3 or 4 round up to 5, 6 or 7 round down to 5, and 8 or 9 round up to 10. Card payments are not rounded.

faq.q: How can my child check if an answer is reasonable?
faq.a: Round the numbers and work out an estimate in your head first. If 4 × 76 gives 2824 but 4 × 80 = 320, the answer is far too big and should be checked.

items.e: 47 is between 40 and 50. Look at the ones digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 50.

items.q: Round 83 to the nearest 10.
items.e: 83 is between 80 and 90. Look at the ones digit: 3. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 80.

items.e: 365 is exactly halfway between 360 and 370. A number exactly halfway rounds up. Answer: 370.

items.q: Round 2995 to the nearest 10.
items.e: 2995 is exactly halfway between 2990 and 3000. A number exactly halfway rounds up. The tens digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 tens. Regroup them as 1 hundred. Answer: 3000.

items.q: Round 340 to the nearest 100.
items.e: 340 is between 300 and 400. Look at the tens digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 300.

items.q: Round 682 to the nearest 100.

items.q: Round 1749 to the nearest 100.
items.e: 1749 is between 1700 and 1800. Look at the tens digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Do not round in steps (1749 → 1750 → 1800); look only at the tens digit. Answer: 1700.

items.q: Round 3962 to the nearest 100.
items.e: 3962 is between 3900 and 4000. Look at the tens digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up. The hundreds digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 hundreds. Regroup them as 1 thousand. Answer: 4000.

items.q: Round 5050 to the nearest 100.
items.e: 5050 is exactly halfway between 5000 and 5100. A number exactly halfway rounds up. Answer: 5100.

items.q: Which number rounds to 500 when you round to the nearest 100?

items.e: 4682 is between 4000 and 5000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 5000.

items.e: 6499 is between 6000 and 7000. Look at the hundreds digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Do not round in steps (6499 → 6500 → 7000); look only at the hundreds digit. Answer: 6000.

items.q: Round 9615 to the nearest 1000.
items.e: 9615 is between 9000 and 10 000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 thousands. Regroup them as 1 ten thousand. Answer: 10 000.

items.q: Round 3087 to the nearest 1000.
items.e: 3087 is between 3000 and 4000. Look at the hundreds digit: 0. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 3000.

sets.title: Money: round, estimate and pay cash

items.q: A pack of stickers costs $3.45. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $3.45 is between $3 and $4. Look at the cents: 45c is less than 50c, so round down to $3.

items.q: A pair of thongs costs $7.50. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $7.50 is exactly halfway between $7 and $8. Halfway rounds up, so $8.

items.q: A beach towel costs $12.95. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $12.95 is between $12 and $13. Look at the cents: 95c is more than 50c, so round up to $13.

items.q: A notebook costs $6.08. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $6.08 is between $6 and $7. Look at the cents: 8c is less than 50c, so round down to $6.

items.q: A cricket ball costs $19.50. What is the price to the nearest dollar?
items.e: $19.50 is exactly halfway between $19 and $20. Halfway rounds up, so $20.

items.q: Round each price to the nearest dollar. Estimate the total cost.
items.e: Round each price to the nearest dollar: $3 + $4 + $2 = $9. (The exact total is $8.80.)

items.q: Round each price to the nearest dollar. Estimate the total cost.
items.e: Round each price to the nearest dollar: $3 + $5 + $6 = $14. (The exact total is $14.25.)

items.q: Round each price to the nearest dollar. Estimate the total cost.
items.e: Round each price to the nearest dollar: $13 + $19 + $2 = $34. (The exact total is $33.90.)

items.q: Round each price to the nearest dollar. Estimate the total cost.
items.e: Round each price to the nearest dollar: $25 + $9 + $15 = $49. (The exact total is $48.85.)

items.q: Cooper has $50 at the shops. He wants to buy a lunch box for $12.95, a drink bottle for $18.40 and a pencil case for $9.60. Is $50 enough? Estimate to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest dollar: $13 + $18 + $10 = $41. $41 is less than $50, so yes, it is enough. (The exact total is $40.95.)

items.q: Ruby has $10 at the athletics carnival. She wants to buy a hot dog for $6.50, a juice for $3.80 and an ice block for $2.90. Is $10 enough? Estimate to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest dollar: $7 + $4 + $3 = $14. $14 is more than $10, so no, it is not enough. (The exact total is $13.20.)

items.q: Mei has $20 at the book fair. She wants to buy a book for $14.99 and a colouring book for $8.25. Is $20 enough? Estimate to decide.
items.e: Round to the nearest dollar: $15 + $8 = $23. $23 is more than $20, so no, it is not enough. (The exact total is $23.24.)

items.q: At the school canteen a sandwich and a juice cost $4.37. Noah pays cash, so the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much does he pay?
items.e: Look at the last digit of the cents: 7 rounds down to 5. $4.37 is closer to $4.35 than to $4.40, so he pays $4.35.

items.q: At the sausage sizzle a family buys lunch for $6.91. Ethan pays cash, so the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much does he pay?
items.e: Look at the last digit of the cents: 1 rounds down to 0. $6.91 is closer to $6.90 than to $6.95, so he pays $6.90.

items.q: At the newsagent a pen and a card cost $3.48. Oliver pays cash, so the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much does he pay?
items.e: Look at the last digit of the cents: 8 rounds up to 10. $3.48 is closer to $3.50 than to $3.45, so he pays $3.50.

items.q: At the supermarket the shopping costs $12.93. William pays cash, so the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much does he pay?
items.e: Look at the last digit of the cents: 3 rounds up to 5. $12.93 is closer to $12.95 than to $12.90, so he pays $12.95.

items.q: Lachlan’s shopping comes to $6.42. He pays cash with a $10 note, so the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much change does he get?
items.e: First round the total to the nearest 5c: $6.42 → $6.40. Then $10 − $6.40 = $3.60.

items.q: Mia’s shopping comes to $13.47. She pays cash with a $20 note, so the total is rounded to the nearest 5c. How much change does she get?
items.e: First round the total to the nearest 5c: $13.47 → $13.45. Then $20 − $13.45 = $6.55.

items.q: Liam buys 4 packs of footy cards at $2.95 each. The calculator shows $118.00. Is this reasonable?
items.e: $2.95 rounds to $3. 4 × $3 = $12, so $118.00 is not reasonable. The exact total is $11.80; the decimal point was put in the wrong place.

items.q: Dad buys bread for $4.95, cheese for $7.20 and grapes for $2.85. The receipt says $15.00. Is this reasonable?
items.e: Round: $5 + $7 + $3 = $15. $15.00 is close to $15, so it is reasonable. (Rounding every price down gives $4 + $7 + $2 = $13, which is too low.)
